on cherche à expliquer de manière anecdotique
le pic d'indispo courant 2018.

On se propose de réduire le nombre de catégories en se focalisant sur celles qui drivent les plus grosses variations. On fusionne donc toutes les catégories hydrauliques et l'on se débarrasse de Biomass.


```{r}
by_plant_indispo <- long_format_ENTSOE_indispo %>% 
  group_by(indispo_day, plant_type) %>% 
  summarise(Installed.Capacity = sum(as.numeric(Installed.Capacity)),
            Unavailable.Capacity = sum(as.numeric(Unavailable.Capacity))) %>%
  ungroup()%>% 
  filter(indispo_day > start_date)

tot_unavailability <- final_indispo %>% 
  select(indispo_day, Unavailable.Capacity)%>%
  rename(total_unavailability = Unavailable.Capacity)

by_plant_tot_indispo <- merge(by_plant_indispo, tot_unavailability , by="indispo_day")

by_plant_tot_indispo <- by_plant_tot_indispo %>% 
  mutate(share = Unavailable.Capacity/total_unavailability)

colnames(by_plant_tot_indispo)

# Define the hydro-related plant types
hydro_types <- c("Hydro Pumped Storage", "Hydro Run-of-river and poundage", "Hydro Water Reservoir")

final_by_plant_tot_indispo <- by_plant_tot_indispo %>%
  group_by(indispo_day) %>% 
  # Summarize the hydro-related rows into a single "Hydro" row
  filter(plant_type %in% hydro_types) %>%
  summarise(across(c(share, Installed.Capacity, Unavailable.Capacity, total_unavailability), sum, na.rm = TRUE),
            plant_type = "Hydro") %>%
  # Bind this new "Hydro" row with the rest of the data, excluding original hydro-related rows
  bind_rows(by_plant_tot_indispo %>% filter(!plant_type %in% hydro_types))%>% 
  ungroup() %>% 
  arrange(indispo_day)

other_types <- c("Other", "Biomass")
final_by_plant_tot_indispo <- final_by_plant_tot_indispo %>%
  group_by(indispo_day) %>% 
  filter(plant_type %in% other_types) %>%
  summarise(across(c(share, Installed.Capacity, Unavailable.Capacity, total_unavailability), sum, na.rm = TRUE),
            plant_type = "Others") %>%
  # Bind this new "Hydro" row with the rest of the data, excluding original hydro-related rows
  bind_rows(final_by_plant_tot_indispo %>% filter(!plant_type %in% other_types))%>% 
  ungroup() %>% 
  arrange(indispo_day)



```


Get customized legend
```{r}
library(ggplot2)
# fake plot just to construct the correct legend
colors_plant <- c("blue", "red", "green", "yellow", "purple","orange")
names <- unique(final_by_plant_tot_indispo$plant_type)

# Define plant types as a factor with specified levels to control the order
example_data <- data.frame(
  V1 = rnorm(100),  # Random numeric values
  plant_type = factor(sample(names, 100, replace = TRUE), levels = names)  # Factor with levels
)

plot_legend <- ggplot(data =example_data, aes(x=V1, fill = plant_type))+
  geom_histogram()+
  theme( legend.direction = "horizontal")+
scale_fill_manual(
  values = colors_plant,
  labels = rev(names))
# Légende personnalisée (à ajuster selon vos besoins)
custom_legend <- cowplot::get_legend(plot_legend)
plot_legend
```



On regarde l'évolution de la composition des indispos 

```{r}
# Reshaper les données en format long pour ggplot2


  # long_data <- pivot_longer(decomp_tot_data, 
  #                           cols = -time, names_to = "category",
  #                           values_to = "value")

  # S'assurer que 'category' a l'ordre des niveaux correspondant à 'colors_shock'
  # Modifier l'ordre des niveaux du facteur category
final_by_plant_tot_indispo$plant_type <- factor(final_by_plant_tot_indispo$plant_type, levels = unique(final_by_plant_tot_indispo$plant_type))
  
colnames(by_plant_tot_indispo)
  # Tracer des barres empilées avec ggplot2
  my_plot <- ggplot()+
    geom_bar(data= final_by_plant_tot_indispo, aes(x = indispo_day, y = share, fill = plant_type),
             stat = "identity", position = "stack") +  # Barres empilées
    scale_fill_manual(
      values = rev(colors_plant),
      labels = rev(names))+

    labs(title= "Share of Unavailability by Plant Type" ,
         x="Time", y="Contribution")+
    theme(legend.position = "none")

my_plot
   
final_plot_with_title <- plot_grid(my_plot ,custom_legend, ncol = 1, rel_heights = c(1, 0.2))

# Display the final plot
print(final_plot_with_title)
```

On veut faire le même graphique non en %,
mais en valeur absolue

```{r}
my_plot <- ggplot()+
    geom_bar(data= final_by_plant_tot_indispo, aes(x = indispo_day, y = Unavailable.Capacity, fill = plant_type),
             stat = "identity", position = "stack") +  # Barres empilées
    scale_fill_manual(
      values = rev(colors_plant),
      labels = rev(names))+

    labs(title= "Unavailability by Plant Type" ,
         x="Time", y="Contribution")+
    theme(legend.position = "none")
   
final_plot_with_title <- plot_grid(my_plot ,custom_legend, ncol = 1, rel_heights = c(1, 0.2))

# Display the final plot
print(final_plot_with_title)
```
